_comment: MINIMAL questions-only bundle. Only subject + chapter_title are required. The ingester finds the chapter automatically; if it's ambiguous (e.g. NIOS and CBSE both have a 'Physics' subject with a 'Motion in a Plane' chapter), the error message lists the candidates and asks you to add a `board` or `class_level` disambiguator.

meta.author: Subject teacher
meta.notes: Just adding practice questions; no summary / lesson plan / worksheet etc. for now.

questions.question: On level ground, the range of a projectile is maximum at a launch angle of
questions.explanation: R = u² sin 2θ / g; sin 2θ is maximum at 2θ = 90°.

questions.question: A projectile launched at 20 m/s at 30° has a time of flight of (g = 10 m/s²)
In uniform circular motion, the speed is constant but the velocity changes.
questions.explanation: Speed is the magnitude of velocity; direction changes continuously even though magnitude is fixed.

questions.question: The centripetal acceleration of a particle moving at speed v in a circle of radius r is ____.
questions.explanation: a_c = v²/r = ω²r, directed toward the centre.

questions.question: Explain why uniform circular motion is accelerated motion, even though the speed is constant.
questions.answer: Acceleration tracks the change in velocity (a vector), not speed (a scalar). In uniform circular motion the direction of velocity changes continuously, so the velocity vector is changing — there is a centripetal acceleration v²/r directed toward the centre.
